title: Request Context Orchestrator: unified SDK middleware for cross-service trace continuity
creator: Maya R. Chen
description:
Problem: We continue to see fragmented traces in multi-host, mixed-language flows (Node server -> Python worker -> Go aggregator, plus WebSocket streams and edge workers). Inconsistent header formats, duplicated baggage, and runtime-specific context loss (async/task queues, fiber pools) make root-cause analysis difficult and inflate MTTR.

Goal: Build a Request Context Orchestrator (RCO) as a small, framework-agnostic middleware surface across our SDKs and a lightweight normalization gateway for inbound traffic. The RCO will: 1) normalize incoming trace headers (W3C, legacy Redwood envelope) into a single canonical context; 2) expose a tiny, zero-allocation context accessor for hot paths; 3) provide deterministic sampling reconciliation and sticky decision propagation; 4) support explicit context stitching across async boundaries (jobs, websockets, worker pools).

Scope & ship strategy:
- Phase 1 (design + PoC): define canonical context model and header precedence rules, add Node and Python SDK middleware that implement normalization and a minimal in-proc context cache. Provide opt-in config flags and feature gates.
- Phase 2 (integration): gRPC/HTTP gateway header normalizer (sidecar mode optional), add support in Go SDK, and implement synthetics to validate continuity across languages.
- Phase 3 (rollout): canary on infra-critical services, dashboards to track trace continuity metrics and perf regressions, automatic fallback to original headers if reconstruction fails.

Compatibility & API: RCO will preserve original headers in a reserved attribute ("raw_propagation_headers") to avoid losing forensic signals. SDK API will be tiny: attachContext(req, ctx) and getContext(). Middleware will attempt to be zero-blocking; any heavier reconstruction will be offloaded to a background queue.

Trade-offs & risks:
- Normalization can obscure original header forms; mitigation: retain raw headers as attributes and log when normalization changes values.
- Slight CPU/regression risk in high-throughput services; mitigation: microbenchmarks, use fast-path (no allocations) for common case, and opt-in slow-path for legacy compatibility.
- Sampling reconciliation across domains may change observed sample rate; mitigation: tie sampling policy to customer tier and expose telemetry.

Observability & acceptance criteria:
- Add dashboard cards: "trace_continuity_rate" (percentage of requests with end-to-end single trace id), "context_drop_rate", and p99 propagation latency.
- Synthetic test suite that covers HTTP->WS->job->grpc flows; target >99.5% continuity on canary.
- Performance target: median request overhead < 250us in 95th percentile common case; p99 overhead < 1ms.
- Telemetry available in Console with per-service breakdown and a rollout flag for automatic rollback on regressions.

Artifacts & links:
- RFC: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/RCO+RFC
- Prototype PR (Node): https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/4123
- Gateway proposal: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1RCO-gateway-proposal

Next steps: finalize RFC comments by 2026-02-16, merge PoC by 2026-02-28, and start canary deployment on staging infra by 2026-03-10.
